question: Two trains having lengths of 210 m and 440 m are running at speeds of 60 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 210 + 440 = 650 m.

Relative speed (same direction) = 90 − 60 = 30 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 30 × (5 / 18) = 25 / 3 m/s.

Time to cross = Distance ÷ Speed = 650 × (3 / 25) = 78 seconds.

Time in minutes = 78 ÷ 60 = 1.3 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.3 minutes.**

 Trains Moving in Same Direction

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 210 m

Length of faster train (L₂) = 440 m

Speed of slower train (V₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of faster train (V₂) = 90 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = V₂ − V₁

Time to cross = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 210 + 440 = 650 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 90 − 60 = 30 km/h

⇒ Convert speed to m/s = 30 × (5 / 18) = 150 / 18 = 25 / 3 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 650 ÷ (25 / 3) = 650 × (3 / 25)

⇒ Time taken = 26 × 3 = 78 seconds

⇒ Convert time to minutes = 78 ÷ 60 = 1.3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 1.3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Trains Crossing

When a train completely crosses another train (whether moving or stationary) or a platform, the total distance covered to clear each other is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by (5 / 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 / 5).
